analysis:
All three changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/...). No production code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation or authorization paths are modified in the supplied units.

SystemMemoryTests.swift: tests were rewritten for a new SystemMemory.availableBytes(stats:pageSize:policy:) signature with a page-cache-aware reclaimable measure (max of free+inactive and free+file-backed+purgeable). The production change is not in this batch, so the new reclaimable credit for page cache cannot be verified here. The tests show that freeOnly stays fail-closed (nil stats, pageSize .max or 0 return 0) and that anonymous, compressed and wired memory earn no extra credit. One case at line 219 shows reclaimable with pageSize .max returns .max, which is an unchecked overflow-saturation contract in the production sampler. This is an availability/admission concern (T-029 and memory-admission class), not a confidentiality regression, and it needs checking in the SystemMemory source. The default policy remains reclaimable and an invalid env value maps to freeOnly (fail-closed), both unchanged.

GLM5NextLogprobsTests.swift (added): gated by DARKBLOOM_TEST_GLM5_MANAGED_SYNTHETIC. It exercises the logprobs channel on the native GLM engine, with cacheEnabled false and an isolated cache directory. It does not touch T-041 at-rest cache surfaces. The test expectation that logprob rows never draft MTP is a functional check only.

GLM5NextManagedLoadTests.swift: adds think tokens to the synthetic tokenizer fixture, and a test that verifiedArtifactSHA256 is set only after every manifest file verifies and stays nil for a same-size corrupted shard. This supports T-012/T-027 weight-integrity expectations. The production property is only tested here, not shown.

The next pass should confirm that the production SystemMemory change is bounded (no overflow, uses a correct file-backed count) and that verifiedArtifactSHA256 is only published after full verification.
